title: You 2.0: The Gift of Other People

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, Madison Avenue was trying to come up with a campaign for a major consumer brand.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代，麦迪逊大道正在为某个大型消费品牌构思广告宣传活动。

sentences.en: On a ranch in Wyoming, advertising executives discovered a cowboy who seemed like a perfect fit.
sentences.zh: 在怀俄明州的一个牧场里，广告主管们发现了一位看起来非常合适的牛仔。

sentences.en: His name was Daryl Winfield, and he came across as tough, masculine, self-reliant.
sentences.zh: 他叫达里尔·温菲尔德，给人的印象是坚毅、阳刚、自立。

sentences.en: His face was soon plastered on billboards across America, Asia, and Africa.
sentences.zh: 很快，他的脸就出现在了美国、亚洲和非洲各地的广告牌上。

sentences.en: Ads showed him riding across rugged landscapes, often in silhouette.
sentences.zh: 广告画面中，他经常以剪影的形式骑马穿行在崎岖的风景中。

sentences.en: As violence played hauntingly in the background, the slogan on screen read,
sentences.zh: 伴随着萦绕心头的背景音乐，屏幕上打出了这样的标语：

sentences.en: This is Marlboro Country.
sentences.zh: 这就是万宝路的世界。

sentences.en: The campaign to sell Marlboro cigarettes was one of the most effective in the history of advertising.
sentences.zh: 这场推销万宝路香烟的广告活动是广告史上最有效的宣传之一。

sentences.en: It sold more than just tobacco products.
sentences.zh: 它销售的不仅仅是烟草产品。

sentences.en: It sold an image of the American WeSt.
sentences.zh: 它销售的是一种美国西部的形象。

sentences.en: In urban neighborhoods across the United States, and in crowded cities and poor villages around the world,
sentences.zh: 在美国各地的城市街区，以及世界各地的拥挤城市和贫困村庄里，

sentences.en: it offered a seductive vision of independence, self-sufficiency, and freedom.
sentences.zh: 它提供了一种关于独立、自给自足和自由的诱人愿景。

sentences.en: The Marlboro Man told two great lies.
sentences.zh: 万宝路牛仔讲述了两个弥天大谎。

sentences.en: The first caused untold sickness, disease, and death.
sentences.zh: 第一个谎言导致了难以言说的疾病、痛苦和死亡。

sentences.en: Cigarettes are responsible for millions of deaths from lung cancer, heart disease, and emphysema.
sentences.zh: 香烟是导致数百万人死于肺癌、心脏病和肺气肿的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: But our story today is about the second great lie.
sentences.zh: 但我们今天的故事是关于第二个弥天大谎。

sentences.en: The Marlboro Man, and countless other media creations like it,
sentences.zh: 万宝路牛仔以及无数其他类似的媒体创作，

sentences.en: suggest that our best lives are lived when we can be free of the cares, the concerns, and the constraints of other people.
sentences.zh: 都在暗示我们：只有摆脱他人的牵挂、关注和束缚，我们才能过上最好的生活。

sentences.en: Today, we unpack how those themes have been woven into our lives,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将剖析这些主题是如何融入我们的生活，

sentences.en: in the attitudes we have, and in the choices we make.
sentences.zh: 融入我们的态度，以及我们所做的选择之中的。

sentences.en: It's also the start of our annual summer series, U2.0.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们年度夏季系列节目“U2.0”的开篇。

sentences.en: As we do every year, we will share ideas and wisdom that can help you to thrive and to grow.
sentences.zh: 像往年一样，我们将分享一些能帮助你茁壮成长和进步的理念与智慧。

sentences.en: Unlocking the science of meaningful relationships.
sentences.zh: 解锁有意义的人际关系背后的科学。

sentences.en: This week, on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周，在《隐藏的大脑》节目中。

sentences.en: Psychologists and social scientists have wrestled with the themes of connection and independence for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，心理学家和社会科学家一直在探讨联系与独立这两个主题。

sentences.en: Human beings need one another and crave friendship and social approval.
sentences.zh: 人类需要彼此，渴望友谊和社会认可。

sentences.en: But we also value solitude, silence, and being left alone in peace.
sentences.zh: 但我们也珍视孤独、宁静，以及不被打扰的安宁。

sentences.en: At the University of Chicago, psychologist Nicholas Epley has spent many years thinking about this tension.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥大学，心理学家尼古拉斯·埃普利多年来一直在思考这种张力。

sentences.en: He has come up with innovative ways we can be the best version of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一些创新的方法，让我们能够成为最好的自己。

sentences.en: Nick Epley, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 尼克·埃普利，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Nick, you live on the outskirts of Chicago, and you take a long train ride into the city to go to work every day.
sentences.zh: 尼克，你住在芝加哥郊外，每天都要坐很长时间的火车进城上班。

sentences.en: For years, you followed an unvarying protocol on the train.
sentences.zh: 多年来，你在火车上一直遵循着一套不变的规矩。

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做的？

sentences.en: Oh, I just sat there and ignored everybody.
sentences.zh: 哦，我只是坐在那里，无视所有人。

sentences.en: I'd read a book, I'd listen to music, I'd scroll through my phone looking at the news.
sentences.zh: 我会看书、听音乐，或者刷手机看新闻。

sentences.en: The kind of thing that everybody else does.
sentences.zh: 就是每个人都会做的那种事。

sentences.en: You sit down, you leave other people alone.
sentences.zh: 你坐下来，不去打扰别人。

sentences.en: So, one morning many years ago, you stepped onto the train as usual, but something struck you for the first time.
sentences.zh: 那么，多年前的一个早晨，你像往常一样上了火车，但有什么东西第一次触动了你。

sentences.en: What did you find yourself thinking about that day, Nick?
sentences.zh: 那天你发现自己在想些什么，尼克？

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember this day like a lightning bolt to the brain.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得那天就像一道闪电击中了大脑。

sentences.en: I actually had been on that particular day writing a chapter describing how we're made happier and healthier by reaching out and connecting with others, by being social.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那天我正在写一章内容，描述我们如何通过主动接触和联系他人，通过社交，变得更快乐、更健康。

sentences.en: And yet, I kind of looked up that morning and realized for the first time, it just kind of hit me, that here we are,
sentences.zh: 然而，那天早上我抬头看了一眼，第一次意识到，它就这样击中了我：我们在这里，

sentences.en: highly social creatures with brains uniquely adapted for connecting to the minds of others.
sentences.zh: 作为高度社会化的生物，我们的大脑天生就是为了与他人的思想建立联系而进化的。

sentences.en: And yet, we're all sitting here ignoring each other.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却都坐在这里，无视彼此。

sentences.en: And that struck me as bizarre.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得很荒谬。

sentences.en: I guess no one really wants to be that guy that opens up a conversation that's an unwanted conversation.
sentences.zh: 我想没人真的想成为那种开启一段不受欢迎对话的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That guy that makes you want to put a pencil through your ear or wish you brought headphones with you.
sentences.zh: 就是那种让你想拿铅笔戳进耳朵，或者希望自己带了耳机的人。

sentences.en: You know, that guy who drives you nuts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种让你抓狂的人。

sentences.en: And so, people sit there and are quiet.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们坐在那里，保持安静。

sentences.en: So, on this day you get on the train, you notice the contrast between what you're writing about in the book and what you're seeing in the train compartment.
sentences.zh: 所以，那天你上了火车，注意到了你书中所写的内容与你在车厢里看到的情景之间的反差。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I decided to run an experiment that day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我决定那天做一个实验。

sentences.en: I essentially enrolled myself in my own experiment, at least as a sample of one.
sentences.zh: 我基本上把自己注册进了我自己的实验中，至少作为一个样本。

sentences.en: And I decided I'd try to have a conversation with somebody that morning.
sentences.zh: 我决定那天早上试着和某人交谈。

sentences.en: I'd take an interest in somebody else.
sentences.zh: 我要对别人表现出兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm not – I'm probably not the most inviting-looking person.
sentences.zh: 我不是——我可能不是那种看起来最容易让人接近的人。

sentences.en: I'm kind of a big guy.
sentences.zh: 我个子挺大的。

sentences.en: I'm a man.
sentences.zh: 我是个男人。

sentences.en: And so, typically, people will get on the train and they'll take the seats that are open eventually until there are no seats left,
sentences.zh: 所以，通常人们上火车后会坐空位，直到没有座位为止，

sentences.en: at which point somebody will have to sit next to me.
sentences.zh: 到那时，就不得不有人坐在我旁边了。

sentences.en: So, eventually, all the seats are taken and a woman comes and sits down next to me.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终所有的座位都坐满了，一位女士走过来坐在我旁边。

sentences.en: She's an African-American woman in probably her mid-50s or so, I would guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜她是一位非裔美国女性，大概50多岁。

sentences.en: She had on a bright red hat.
sentences.zh: 她戴着一顶鲜红色的帽子。

sentences.en: I remember that very vividly.
sentences.zh: 我记得非常清楚。

sentences.en: She sat down next to me and I decided I'm going to try to get to know a little something about her.
sentences.zh: 她坐在我旁边，我决定试着去了解她一点点。

sentences.en: And so, I said the first thing that came to my mind, which was a joke but a compliment at the same time.
sentences.zh: 于是，我说了脑海中浮现的第一句话，那既是一个玩笑，同时也是一个恭维。

sentences.en: I complimented her on her hat.
sentences.zh: 我称赞了她的帽子。

sentences.en: I said how much I liked it and that I had one just like it.
sentences.zh: 我说我很喜欢它，而且我正好也有一顶一模一样的。

sentences.en: And we both chuckled.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都笑了。

sentences.en: I mean, it wasn't – look, it's probably not the best joke you've ever heard.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那并不是——听着，这可能不是你听过最好的笑话。

sentences.en: But that got the conversation started.
sentences.zh: 但那让对话开始了。

sentences.en: And from there, it just went.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，对话就自然而然地进行了下去。

sentences.en: We talked about our careers and our jobs and what we did for a living.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了各自的职业、工作以及我们靠什么谋生。

sentences.en: But also, whether this was really what we wanted to do for a living.
sentences.zh: 但也聊到了这是否真的是我们想做的工作。

sentences.en: I remember her feeling sort of stuck in her job and wasn't quite what she wanted to do and thinking about making a change.
sentences.zh: 我记得她感觉自己在工作中有些受困，那并不是她真正想做的事，她正在考虑做出改变。

sentences.en: She talked a little bit about her family, how she needed to support her family.
sentences.zh: 她聊了一些关于她家人的事，谈到她需要养家糊口。

sentences.en: And, you know, the conversation went really faSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对话进行得非常快。

sentences.en: It was about a half an hour trip.
sentences.zh: 那是一段大约半小时的旅程。

sentences.en: I was over really quickly.
sentences.zh: 很快就结束了。

sentences.en: I was struck by that.
sentences.zh: 我对此印象深刻。

sentences.en: And as I got up to leave, I thanked her for taking time to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 当我起身离开时，我感谢她花时间和我聊天。

sentences.en: She seemed delighted to have talked to me.
sentences.zh: 她似乎很高兴能和我交谈。

sentences.en: And as I walked off the train, I remembered two feelings.
sentences.zh: 当我走下火车时，我记住了两种感觉。

sentences.en: One, that it felt nice and was nicer than what I'd have normally done that morning, which was probably scroll through the news.
sentences.zh: 第一，感觉很好，而且比我那天早上通常会做的事——可能就是刷新闻——要好得多。

sentences.en: But the other thing I remembered was that it was surprisingly nice.
sentences.zh: 但另一件事我记得的是，这种感觉好得令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I was surprised by that, surprised by how nice it was.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到惊讶，惊讶于它竟然如此美好。

sentences.en: There was another time in Nick's life when he found himself surprised by the effect of talking to strangers.
sentences.zh: 尼克的生活中还有一次，他发现自己对与陌生人交谈的效果感到惊讶。

sentences.en: He and his wife, Jen, were expecting a baby.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子简当时正在期待一个孩子的降生。

sentences.en: Doctors had run some tests and told Nick that his daughter was likely going to have a genetic disorder.
sentences.zh: 医生做了一些检查，告诉尼克他的女儿很可能患有某种遗传疾病。

sentences.en: I remember Jen met me in the breezeway of the house when I got home, and she told me that it was likely that our daughter had Down syndrome.
sentences.zh: 我记得我回家时，简在门廊迎接我，她告诉我我们的女儿很可能患有唐氏综合症。

sentences.en: And I remember it almost felt like I was hit in the cheSt.
sentences.zh: 我记得那感觉就像胸口挨了一拳。

sentences.en: I kind of fell back against the wall.
sentences.zh: 我整个人向后倒在墙上。

sentences.en: It was a shock.
sentences.zh: 那是一个打击。

sentences.en: It was unexpected.
sentences.zh: 那是意料之外的。

sentences.en: At first, all that Nick wanted was to be left alone with his shock and confusion.
sentences.zh: 起初，尼克只想独自一人面对他的震惊和困惑。

sentences.en: He couldn't bear to talk to anyone else.
sentences.zh: 他无法忍受与任何人交谈。

sentences.en: Whenever you experience a shock like this, you look inward.
sentences.zh: 每当你经历这样的打击时，你都会向内审视。

sentences.en: It's a little bit hard to reach out to people, not quite sure what to talk about or what to say.
sentences.zh: 向别人倾诉有点困难，不太确定该聊些什么或说些什么。

sentences.en: And so my first instinct was to try to figure this out myself, figure out what best to do, how best to approach this.
sentences.zh: 所以我的第一直觉是试着自己解决这个问题，弄清楚最好的应对方法，最好的处理方式。

sentences.en: In time, however, Nick and Jen did reach out to other parents who had children with special needs.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着时间的推移，尼克和简确实向其他有特殊需求孩子的父母寻求了帮助。

sentences.en: They quickly discovered that strangers were not only willing to talk, but had insights that felt surprisingly useful.
sentences.zh: 他们很快发现，陌生人不仅愿意交谈，而且还提供了令人惊讶的有用见解。

sentences.en: It was actually pretty stunning.
sentences.zh: 这实际上相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: Pretty much every person we talked to, at some point in the conversation, used the same word to describe their experience.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈过的几乎每个人，在对话的某个时刻，都用了同一个词来描述他们的经历。

sentences.en: They all, at some point, used the word blessing to describe the experience of having a child with Down syndrome, that they all considered it to be a major blessing in their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们在某个时刻都用了“祝福”这个词来描述抚养唐氏综合症孩子的经历，他们都认为这是他们生命中重大的祝福。

sentences.en: One that opened their eyes to a new way of living that they hadn't seen before, that gave them a new perspective on life that they hadn't had before,
sentences.zh: 它让他们大开眼界，看到了一种以前从未见过的新生活方式，给了他们一种以前从未有过的生活视角，

sentences.en: that brought their family together in a way they would not have guessed before.
sentences.zh: 并以一种他们之前无法预料的方式让他们的家庭更加团结。

sentences.en: And for me, hearing these stories from these families, hearing what it was actually like, getting their perspective directly,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，听到这些家庭的故事，听到他们真实的感受，直接获得他们的视角，

sentences.en: was very reassuring for me to know that we could do this.
sentences.zh: 让我感到非常安心，知道我们能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: Six months into the pregnancy, Jen suffered a miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 怀孕六个月时，简流产了。

sentences.en: Both she and Nick were devastated.
sentences.zh: 她和尼克都悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: Again, they turned to others for guidance and perspective.
sentences.zh: 他们再次向他人寻求指导和视角。

sentences.en: In a few months, based on the experience of other parents who had suffered similar tragedies,
sentences.zh: 几个月后，基于其他经历过类似悲剧的父母的经验，

sentences.en: they decided to do something they would not have dreamed of doing months earlier.
sentences.zh: 他们决定做一件几个月前想都不敢想的事情。

sentences.en: They decided to adopt a child with Down syndrome.
sentences.zh: 他们决定领养一个患有唐氏综合症的孩子。

sentences.en: Jen had done some research and learned that it might be possible to adopt a child from China.
sentences.zh: 简做了一些研究，了解到从中国领养一个孩子可能是可行的。

sentences.en: There's quite a community of people who have done this.
sentences.zh: 有一个相当大的群体做过这件事。

sentences.en: And we had a lot of conversations before we moved ahead with this.
sentences.zh: 在我们推进这件事之前，我们进行了很多次对话。

sentences.en: But I would say not so much to reassure us that this was the right thing for us to do at this time,
sentences.zh: 但我会说，与其说是为了让我们确信这是我们当时应该做的正确的事，

sentences.en: but rather to learn more about how this would actually happen and how long this would take.
sentences.zh: 不如说是为了更多地了解这件事会如何发生，以及需要多长时间。

sentences.en: And did you end up adopting a child from China?
sentences.zh: 那你最终从中国领养了一个孩子吗？

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's a blessing, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 她是一个祝福，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Her name is Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫琳赛。

sentences.en: She is in first grade.
sentences.zh: 她现在上一年级。

sentences.en: She's eight years old now.
sentences.zh: 她现在八岁了。

sentences.en: This is five years ago that we brought her home.
sentences.zh: 我们把她带回家已经五年了。

sentences.en: We took all of our kids to China when we brought Lindsay home with us.
sentences.zh: 当我们把琳赛带回家时，我们带着所有的孩子去了中国。

sentences.en: And it's been the most amazing thing that Jen and I have done together in our lives so far.
sentences.zh: 这是简和我迄今为止在生活中一起做过的最棒的事情。

sentences.en: I don't think we would have gotten to the position where we were open or yet he even thought about bringing Lindsay into our lives without reaching out and connecting with other people to essentially be reassured that it would not just be something we could do,
sentences.zh: 我不认为如果我们没有主动接触和联系其他人，去获得那种“我们不仅能做到，而且这对我们来说将是一种祝福”的保证，我们就能达到那种开放的状态，甚至不会想到把琳赛带进我们的生活。

sentences.en: but that it would be a blessing for us.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: I keep hearing those words echoing in my mind over and over again that we heard from those families when we talked to them initially.
sentences.zh: 我不断地在脑海中回响着那些话，那些我们最初与那些家庭交谈时听到的词语。

sentences.en: In time, Nick came to see there was a pattern connecting these different stories.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，尼克开始看到这些不同故事之间存在着一种模式。

sentences.en: He fully expected he would feel better when he rode the train in silence, but he felt better when he talked to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 他本以为在火车上保持沉默会感觉更好，但实际上与陌生人交谈让他感觉更好。

sentences.en: He wanted to withdraw into himself when he learned his daughter would have Down syndrome, but when he reached out to strangers,
sentences.zh: 当得知女儿患有唐氏综合症时，他想退缩到自己的世界里，但当他向陌生人寻求帮助时，

sentences.en: those conversations unexpectedly changed the way he felt.
sentences.zh: 那些对话出人意料地改变了他的感受。

sentences.en: He was not someone who imagined adopting a child with special needs, but talking to other people who had done this revealed to him something about himself that he did not know.
sentences.zh: 他原本不是那种会想象领养特殊需求孩子的人，但与那些做过这件事的人交谈，向他揭示了一些他自己都不知道的关于自己的事情。

sentences.en: When we come back, why we so often seek to walk alone or in silence, and the psychology of what happens when we resist this impulse?
sentences.zh: 节目回来后，我们将探讨为什么我们经常寻求独自一人或保持沉默，以及当我们抵制这种冲动时会发生什么的心理学。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When University of Chicago psychologist Nick Epley received word that the baby he and his wife were expecting had Down syndrome,
sentences.zh: 当芝加哥大学心理学家尼克·埃普利得知他和妻子期待的孩子患有唐氏综合症时，

sentences.en: his first impulse was to withdraw from others and go it alone.
sentences.zh: 他的第一冲动是远离他人，独自承担。

sentences.en: But he eventually found great comfort and reassurance by hearing about the experiences of other parents.
sentences.zh: 但最终，通过倾听其他父母的经历，他获得了巨大的安慰和保证。

sentences.en: Over time, Nick came to see that this was not an isolated incident.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，尼克开始明白，这并非孤立事件。

sentences.en: Opportunities for connection present themselves to us every day.
sentences.zh: 连接的机会每天都在我们身边出现。

sentences.en: In his book, Mind Wise, Why We Misunderstand What Others Think, Believe, Feel, and Want,
sentences.zh: 在他的著作《明智：为什么我们误解了他人的想法、信念、感受和欲望》中，

sentences.en: he explores why our assumptions about people are often off base.
sentences.zh: 他探讨了为什么我们对他人的假设往往是错误的。

sentences.en: Nick, you became increasingly curious about a phenomenon that you started to call under-sociality.
sentences.zh: 尼克，你对一种你开始称之为“社交不足”的现象越来越好奇。

sentences.en: What is under-sociality, Nick?
sentences.zh: 尼克，什么是“社交不足”？

sentences.en: So, I'm kind of struck by what seems like a paradox that's right at the core of human life.
sentences.zh: 我被人类生活核心中似乎存在的一个悖论所触动。

sentences.en: That on the one hand, we, as human beings, are deeply social.
sentences.zh: 一方面，作为人类，我们是深度社交的生物。

sentences.en: We're made happier and healthier by reaching out and connecting to other people, whether it's strangers or family and friends.
sentences.zh: 通过接触并与他人建立联系，无论是陌生人还是亲朋好友，我们都会变得更快乐、更健康。

sentences.en: And yet, there are so many opportunities in daily life where we could reach out and connect with other people that we don't take.
sentences.zh: 然而，在日常生活中，我们有太多可以主动接触并与他人建立联系的机会，但我们却错过了。

sentences.en: We have a compliment that comes to our mind that we don't share.
sentences.zh: 我们脑海中闪过一句赞美，却没说出口。

sentences.en: We feel gratitude to somebody that we don't express.
sentences.zh: 我们对某人心存感激，却没表达出来。

sentences.en: We have somebody we could say hello to or talk to or even just smile to that we don't.
sentences.zh: 我们可以向某人问好、交谈，甚至只是微笑，但我们却没有这样做。

sentences.en: We have meaningful things we want to know about other people and we don't ask them about it.
sentences.zh: 我们想了解他人一些有意义的事情，却不去询问。

sentences.en: We don't seem, at least it seemed to me, to be social enough for our own good.
sentences.zh: 至少在我看来，我们似乎并没有为了自己的利益而进行足够的社交。

sentences.en: So, you started running experiments in the Chicago areas where you actually had commuters do what you did on the train that day.
sentences.zh: 所以，你开始在芝加哥地区进行实验，让通勤者做你那天在火车上做的事情。

sentences.en: Walk me through one of these experiments.
sentences.zh: 带我了解一下其中一个实验吧。

sentences.en: What did you ask your volunteers to do and what came of it?
sentences.zh: 你让志愿者们做什么？结果如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the very first one we did was in collaboration with Juliana Schroeder, one of my amazing PhD students at the time, who's now at UC Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们做的第一个实验是与朱莉安娜·施罗德（Juliana Schroeder）合作的，她当时是我出色的博士生之一，现在在加州大学伯克利分校任教。

sentences.en: And we went down to Homewood, Illinois, the Metra train station there, which is actually just one stop to the north of where we live in Flossmoor.
sentences.zh: 我们去了伊利诺伊州霍姆伍德的Metra火车站，那里距离我们居住的弗洛斯穆尔仅一站之遥。

sentences.en: And we set up a sign on the way up to the train platform that recruited people to participate in an experiment if they were interested.
sentences.zh: 我们在通往站台的路上竖起了一个牌子，招募有兴趣的人参加实验。

sentences.en: And we handed them a $5 Starbucks gift card.
sentences.zh: 我们给了他们一张5美元的星巴克礼品卡。

sentences.en: And then we randomly assigned them to do one of three things on the train that morning.
sentences.zh: 然后随机分配他们那天早上在火车上做三件事中的一件。

sentences.en: In one condition, we asked people to just do whatever they normally do on the train.
sentences.zh: 在一种情况下，我们要求人们像往常一样在火车上做他们平时做的事。

sentences.en: In the next condition, this is our solitude condition, we asked people to keep to themselves, to just focus on their day ahead and not engage other people in conversation.
sentences.zh: 在下一种情况下，即我们的“独处”条件，我们要求人们保持独处，专注于自己的一天，不要与他人交谈。

sentences.en: And in the third condition, we asked people to do the thing that I did on the train that morning, which was when somebody comes and sits down next to you,
sentences.zh: 在第三种情况下，我们要求人们做我那天早上在火车上做的事，也就是当有人过来坐在你旁边时，

sentences.en: try to have a conversation.
sentences.zh: 试着进行交谈。

sentences.en: We then handed them an envelope that had their Starbucks gift card in it and a survey in it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们递给他们一个信封，里面装着星巴克礼品卡和一份问卷。

sentences.en: And we told them, at the end of your commute, fill out the survey, drop it back in the mail to us.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他们，在通勤结束时，填好问卷，寄回给我们。

sentences.en: And so off they went.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就出发了。

sentences.en: And what did you find?
sentences.zh: 你们发现了什么？

sentences.en: So we asked them on the survey a few different things.
sentences.zh: 我们在问卷中询问了他们几个不同的问题。

sentences.en: We asked them, how pleasant was your commute compared to normal?
sentences.zh: 我们问他们，与平时相比，你的通勤过程有多愉快？

sentences.en: How happy do you feel after this commute?
sentences.zh: 这次通勤后你感觉有多快乐？

sentences.en: And how sad do you feel?
sentences.zh: 你感觉有多悲伤？

sentences.en: We collapsed these into a single composite, essentially how positive their commute was.
sentences.zh: 我们将这些合并为一个综合指标，本质上就是他们的通勤体验有多积极。

sentences.en: And what we found was that people actually reported having the most positive experience when they talked to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们与陌生人交谈时，他们报告的体验最为积极。

sentences.en: And they had the least positive experience in the solitude condition, where we asked them to keep to themselves.
sentences.zh: 而在我们要求他们保持独处的“独处”条件下，他们的体验最不积极。

sentences.en: The control condition, where people did whatever they normally did, fell in the middle.
sentences.zh: 人们像往常一样行事的对照组处于中间位置。

sentences.en: Although in subsequent experiments, we found that usually that's more like the solitude condition.
sentences.zh: 尽管在随后的实验中，我们发现这种情况通常更接近“独处”条件。

sentences.en: We conducted another experiment where we asked people not to tell us how they actually felt after doing these things,
sentences.zh: 我们进行了另一项实验，要求人们不要告诉我们他们在做这些事情后的真实感受，

sentences.en: but to tell us how they thought they would feel if they were in each of these conditions.
sentences.zh: 而是告诉我们如果他们处于这些条件下，他们认为自己会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: Essentially to predict how they would feel.
sentences.zh: 本质上是预测他们的感受。

sentences.en: And what we found when we did this was that people actually predicted that they would have the least positive experience in the connection condition
sentences.zh: 当我们这样做时，我们发现人们实际上预测自己在“连接”条件下会有最不积极的体验，

sentences.en: and the most positive experience in the control and the solitude condition.
sentences.zh: 而在“对照”和“独处”条件下会有最积极的体验。

sentences.en: And those expectations were just precisely wrong.
sentences.zh: 而这些预期恰恰是错误的。

sentences.en: So you conducted a version of the same study in the London subway system sometime after this.
sentences.zh: 所以后来你在伦敦地铁系统里也进行了同样研究的一个版本。

sentences.en: My understanding is that folks in London want to talk to each other on the train even less than folks in Chicago want to do so.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，伦敦人比芝加哥人更不想在火车上与他人交谈。

sentences.en: Tell me what you found.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你发现了什么。

sentences.en: And I understand that this experiment was coming in the context of some debate about whether people should be talking to one another on trains in London.
sentences.zh: 而且我了解到，这个实验是在关于伦敦火车上人们是否应该交谈的辩论背景下进行的。

sentences.en: Yeah, we were able, through a collaboration with the BBC, to actually run these experiments in a place that's not known for its friendliness, which is London.
sentences.zh: 是的，通过与BBC的合作，我们得以在伦敦这个以“不友好”著称的地方进行了这些实验。

sentences.en: And in fact, not long before we ran this experiment, London tube rider Jonathan Dunn actually started a campaign trying to encourage London tube riders to talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我们进行这项实验前不久，伦敦地铁乘客乔纳森·邓恩（Jonathan Dunn）发起了一场运动，试图鼓励伦敦地铁乘客互相交谈。

sentences.en: He called it tube chat and he handed out buttons and he started a Twitter handle and a Facebook page trying to encourage people to reach out and talk to strangers on the train.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“地铁聊天”（tube chat），分发徽章，还开设了Twitter账号和Facebook页面，试图鼓励人们在火车上主动与陌生人交谈。

sentences.en: And an absolute rebellion ensued.
sentences.zh: 结果引发了一场彻底的叛乱。

sentences.en: There was an alternate Facebook page that was started up, the shut up tube chat campaign, which handed out their own buttons that discourage people from talking to other people.
sentences.zh: 有人建立了一个替代的Facebook页面，即“闭嘴地铁聊天”（shut up tube chat）运动，他们分发自己的徽章，劝阻人们与他人交谈。

sentences.en: Rather drink a pint of bleach than talk to another person?
sentences.zh: 宁愿喝一品脱漂白剂也不愿与人交谈？

sentences.en: Wear this button.
sentences.zh: 戴上这个徽章。

sentences.en: They handed this stuff out.
sentences.zh: 他们分发了这些东西。

sentences.en: So it didn't seem like London was the friendliest place for us to be running these experiments.
sentences.zh: 所以伦敦似乎并不是我们进行这些实验的最友好的地方。

sentences.en: And it turned out that Londoners are human beings, too.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，伦敦人也是人类。

sentences.en: And just like we found in Chicago, those folks who we randomly assigned to be in the connection condition, they reported having the most positive commute.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在芝加哥发现的那样，那些被随机分配到“连接”条件下的参与者，报告说他们的通勤体验最为积极。

sentences.en: And those folks in the control and the solitude conditions reported having the least positive commute.
sentences.zh: 而那些处于“对照”和“独处”条件下的参与者报告说他们的通勤体验最不积极。

sentences.en: Now, hearing about these experiments, I'm imagining that some people will say, you know, extroverted people might enjoy talking to strangers.
sentences.zh: 听到这些实验，我想有些人会说，外向的人可能喜欢和陌生人交谈。

sentences.en: But what about the introverts among us?
sentences.zh: 但我们中间的内向者呢？

sentences.en: Does personality play a role here, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为性格在这里起作用吗？

sentences.en: So we've measured this in these experiments and we don't find that it does.
sentences.zh: 我们在这些实验中测量过这一点，但并没有发现它有影响。

sentences.en: And that's not unique to our research.
sentences.zh: 这在我们的研究中并非个例。

sentences.en: Psychologists have been doing lots of experiments where they ask people to behave more extrovertedly or more introvertedly.
sentences.zh: 心理学家一直在做大量的实验，要求人们表现得更外向或更内向。

sentences.en: And the very consistent finding is that when people actually do this, people feel happier when they act extroverted than when they act introverted.
sentences.zh: 一个非常一致的发现是，当人们真的这样做时，表现得外向的人比表现得内向的人感觉更快乐。

sentences.en: And that's just as true for folks who are consistently extroverted as it is for folks who are consistently introverted.
sentences.zh: 对于那些一贯外向的人和一贯内向的人来说，情况都是如此。

sentences.en: As far as we can tell, where introversion and extroversion matters is not in people's experience of social interaction as much as it is in their choices of social interaction.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，内向和外向的区别不在于人们对社交互动的体验，而在于他们对社交互动的选择。

sentences.en: That is, extroverts choose to reach out and engage with others a little bit more often than introverts do.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，外向者选择主动接触和与他人互动的频率比内向者稍微高一点。

sentences.en: And as a result of choosing to reach out, they tend to be a little bit happier.
sentences.zh: 而由于选择了主动接触，他们往往会稍微快乐一些。

sentences.en: In many ways, it seems a little bit like physical exercise that some of us choose to exercise more than others.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这看起来有点像体育锻炼，我们有些人选择锻炼的次数比其他人多。

sentences.en: Even though all of us, regardless of whether we choose to or not, would actually be a little healthier if we exercised more often.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们所有人，无论是否选择锻炼，如果多锻炼一点，实际上都会更健康。

sentences.en: Same thing seems to be true with our sociality as well.
sentences.zh: 我们的社交活动似乎也是如此。

sentences.en: So if you were to ask me, if I was sitting on the average, you know, bus or plane or train, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你问我，如果我坐在普通的公交车、飞机或火车上，你知道，

sentences.en: how many of the people around me would want to actually have a conversation with me?
sentences.zh: 我周围有多少人真的想和我交谈？

sentences.en: I would not put that number as being very high.
sentences.zh: 我不会把这个数字估计得很高。

sentences.en: I would imagine that most people want to be left to themselves.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人只想独处。

sentences.en: Now, you've actually studied this.
sentences.zh: 你实际上研究过这个问题。

sentences.en: You've actually measured that impressions that people have about how much they think other people want to talk to them.
sentences.zh: 你测量过人们对于“他们认为别人有多想和他们交谈”的印象。

sentences.en: What do you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: So what we find is that this is the big barrier to reaching out and engaging with other people, or at least as one of them,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这是主动接触和与他人互动的一大障碍，或者至少是障碍之一，

sentences.en: is believing that other people don't want to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 那就是认为别人不想和你交谈。

sentences.en: And hence, you might be rejected or this person might be uninterested.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可能会担心被拒绝，或者对方可能不感兴趣。

sentences.en: So on the trains in Chicago and in the subsequent experiment we ran in buses here in Chicago,
sentences.zh: 所以在芝加哥的火车上，以及我们随后在芝加哥公交车上进行的实验中，

sentences.en: people thought less than half of the people on the train would be willing to talk to them if they tried.
sentences.zh: 人们认为如果他们尝试的话，火车上不到一半的人愿意与他们交谈。

sentences.en: In London, it was even more grim.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦，情况甚至更糟。

sentences.en: They thought only about 25% of folks on the trains in London would be willing to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 他们认为伦敦火车上只有约25%的人愿意与你交谈。

sentences.en: Now, with at least believed odds like that, you probably wouldn't try to talk to other people either.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果相信这种几率，你可能也不会尝试与他人交谈。

sentences.en: So I think that helps to explain in part why folks are reluctant to reach out and engage.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这在一定程度上解释了为什么人们不愿意主动接触和互动。

sentences.en: They think other people don't want to.
sentences.zh: 他们认为别人不想这样做。

sentences.en: And so you could get a whole carload of people never trying to talk to somebody else because they think other people don't want to, and then never finding out that they, in fact,
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会看到整整一车厢的人从不尝试与他人交谈，因为他们认为别人不想，结果永远没发现他们其实，

sentences.en: might be wrong about it.
sentences.zh: 可能对此有误解。

sentences.en: So besides underestimating how much we will enjoy a conversation, how positive we'll feel when we talk to strangers,
sentences.zh: 所以除了低估我们从对话中获得的乐趣，以及与陌生人交谈时感受到的积极情绪外，

sentences.en: we also underestimate how much we will learn from a conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们还低估了从对话中能学到多少东西。

sentences.en: What do you find on this front, Nick?
sentences.zh: 尼克，在这方面你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Bill Nye, famous science guy, once said, everyone you will ever meet knows something you don't.
sentences.zh: 著名的科学达人比尔·奈（Bill Nye）曾说，你遇到的每一个人都知道一些你不知道的事情。

sentences.en: And Bill Nye is wise about that.
sentences.zh: 比尔·奈对此很有见地。

sentences.en: Everybody's got a story for you.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有故事可以讲给你听。

sentences.en: Everybody has been through interesting experiences that you haven't been through.
sentences.zh: 每个人都经历过你未曾经历过的有趣体验。

sentences.en: But notice when you look at somebody, you can't see that.
sentences.zh: 但请注意，当你看着某人时，你是看不出这些的。

sentences.en: You see kind of a blank slate.
sentences.zh: 你看到的只是一张白纸。

sentences.en: We don't know what we'll learn.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道我们会学到什么。

sentences.en: And so when we ask people before their conversations with a stranger to anticipate how much they're going to learn in this conversation, we find very consistently that people,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们要求人们在与陌生人交谈前预测他们能从对话中学到多少时，我们非常一致地发现，人们，

sentences.en: they think they're not going to learn a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己学不到太多东西。

sentences.en: And after the conversation, they report learning significantly more both about the person they're talking to, personal details about them, but also about things in general.
sentences.zh: 而对话结束后，他们报告说学到的东西明显更多，既包括关于交谈对象的信息，比如他们的个人细节，也包括一般性的知识。

sentences.en: Whatever it is that you happen to be talking about in the conversation is surprisingly informative.
sentences.zh: 无论你们在对话中谈论什么，内容都出奇地有信息量。

sentences.en: Later in the day I interviewed Nick, I was at a restaurant with friends.
sentences.zh: 那天晚些时候我采访了尼克，当时我和朋友在一家餐馆。

sentences.en: Sitting at the next table were a group of people, and one young man had his son with him.
sentences.zh: 隔壁桌坐着一群人，其中一个年轻人带着他的儿子。

sentences.en: The kid might have been three, and I thought he looked adorable.
sentences.zh: 孩子可能三岁左右，我觉得他看起来很可爱。

sentences.en: I should tell the dad how cute his kid was, I thought.
sentences.zh: 我想，我应该告诉那位父亲他的孩子有多可爱。

sentences.en: Then I said, will it be weird for me to tell a stranger I thought his kid was adorable?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，如果我告诉一个陌生人我觉得他的孩子很可爱，会不会很奇怪？

sentences.en: Nick said something along these lines happened to his own daughter.
sentences.zh: 尼克说类似的事情也发生在他自己的女儿身上。

sentences.en: The two of them were in their kitchen, looking out at the sidewalk in front of their house.
sentences.zh: 他们俩当时在厨房里，看着房子前面的人行道。

sentences.en: And there was a woman who came down the sidewalk who just had this fabulous air, just this beautiful, beautiful afro.
sentences.zh: 有一个女人走过人行道，她有一种极好的气质，留着非常非常漂亮的非洲式发型。

sentences.en: She just looked spectacular.
sentences.zh: 她看起来简直太壮观了。

sentences.en: And Sion commented on it.
sentences.zh: 赛恩（Sion）对此发表了评论。

sentences.en: And I remember standing in the kitchen there telling her, go to the front door and tell her how amazing she looks.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时站在厨房里告诉她，去前门告诉她她看起来有多棒。

sentences.en: And I don't think I could have budged her with a crowbar out of that position.
sentences.zh: 我觉得就算用撬棍我也没法把她从那个位置撬动。

sentences.en: She was just, it was, it just felt so weird to go up and say something like that to somebody, to compliment like that.
sentences.zh: 她只是觉得，去跟别人说那样的话，去那样赞美别人，感觉太奇怪了。

sentences.en: And I think that's another one of these examples of under-sociality.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是“社交不足”的另一个例子。

sentences.en: We have a kind thought come to mind.
sentences.zh: 我们脑海中闪过一个善意的想法。

sentences.en: We could pass it along.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它传达出去。

sentences.en: We'd make them feel great.
sentences.zh: 我们会让他们感觉很棒。

sentences.en: And yet, yeah, it feels a little weird to do that.
sentences.zh: 然而，是的，这样做感觉有点奇怪。

sentences.en: And so maybe we don't.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们没有这样做。

sentences.en: And again, when you put people in a study and in effect, you know, force them to compliment other people, what do you find?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，当你把人们放在一项研究中，实际上，你知道，强迫他们赞美他人时，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: So in these experiments, we ask people who are out together at some public place in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 在这些实验中，我们要求在芝加哥公共场所一起出行的参与者。

sentences.en: We ask one person to write down a compliment about this person that they're with, or sometimes three compliments depending on the experiment we're in,
sentences.zh: 我们要求其中一人写下一句关于同伴的赞美，或者根据实验的不同有时是三句赞美，

sentences.en: that they have just for whatever reason never shared with this person before.
sentences.zh: 这些赞美是他们出于某种原因从未对这个人说过的。

sentences.en: We then ask them to predict how the person's going to feel when they read this compliment or these compliments.
sentences.zh: 然后我们要求他们预测当对方读到这些赞美时会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: We then bring the person they complimented back to read that compliment, and they report how they actually felt about it and also how awkward or weird it was,
sentences.zh: 然后我们带回被赞美的人来阅读这些赞美，他们报告了他们的真实感受，以及这有多尴尬或奇怪，

sentences.en: which was often the barrier, right?
sentences.zh: 这通常就是障碍，对吧？

sentences.en: It's going to be weird to do this.
sentences.zh: 做这件事会很奇怪。

sentences.en: And what we find very consistently is that hearing compliments, even though we know they're going to be positive to the other person, when people actually hear them,
sentences.zh: 我们非常一致地发现，听到赞美，尽管我们知道这对对方来说是积极的，但当人们真的听到时，

sentences.en: when people actually read them, they're even more positive than we expect they'll be.
sentences.zh: 当人们真的读到时，它们比我们预期的要积极得多。

sentences.en: And in fact, this isn't just our research, but great work by Erica Boothby and Vanessa Bones.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这不仅是我们的研究，埃里卡·布斯比（Erica Boothby）和凡妮莎·邦斯（Vanessa Bohns）也做了出色的工作。

sentences.en: They found a similar thing concurrent with us, that when people compliment strangers, they feel better than the compliment givers expect, too.
sentences.zh: 他们和我们同时发现了类似的事情，即当人们赞美陌生人时，他们的感觉比赞美者预期的要好。

sentences.en: The effect seems to be pretty robuSt.
sentences.zh: 这种效应似乎非常稳健。

sentences.en: So there's another form of compliment that many of us are reluctant to offer, and this involves not strangers, but people in our own lives, people we're very close to.
sentences.zh: 所以还有另一种赞美，我们许多人都不愿提供，这不涉及陌生人，而是涉及我们生活中的人，我们非常亲近的人。

sentences.en: And that is the idea of the repeated compliment.
sentences.zh: 那就是重复赞美的想法。

sentences.en: So maybe you thank someone for doing something nice for you, but they do it again the next week and the week after, and after some time, you start to say, well,
sentences.zh: 所以也许你感谢某人为你做的好事，但他们下周又做了，再下周又做了，过了一段时间，你开始说，嗯，

sentences.en: maybe the repeated compliment, you know, it'll sound like it's too much.
sentences.zh: 也许重复的赞美，你知道，听起来会太多了。

sentences.en: You've done research along these lines as well about repeated compliments.
sentences.zh: 你也在这些方面做过关于重复赞美的研究。

sentences.en: What do you find, Nick?
sentences.zh: 尼克，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the fear, of course,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，恐惧在于，

sentences.en: is that you'll start to sound like a broken record if I tell my wife how great she looks and how wonderful her cooking is and how wonderful she is with the kids and how great she is in friendships and whatever.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直告诉妻子她看起来多棒，她的厨艺多好，她对孩子多好，她在友谊中多棒等等，你会开始听起来像一张坏掉的唱片。

sentences.en: I just, you know, you keep giving somebody compliments, eventually it's going to tire.
sentences.zh: 我只是，你知道，你不断地给某人赞美，最终它会让人厌倦。

sentences.en: You're going to adapt to it.
sentences.zh: 你会适应它的。

sentences.en: And it's reasonable to think this because we do kind of adapt to a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这种想法合情合理，因为我们确实会对很多事物产生适应。

sentences.en: In one experiment, we had people write down five compliments to somebody who they were with on a given day, and the next week,
sentences.zh: 在一项实验中，我们让参与者在某一天给他们相处的人写下五句赞美的话，然后在接下来的一周里，

sentences.en: we shared one of those compliments each day with the next person.
sentences.zh: 我们每天与下一个人分享其中一句赞美。

sentences.en: And before sending those compliments out, the people who wrote them anticipated how positive the recipient would feel receiving those compliments.
sentences.zh: 在发送这些赞美之前，写下它们的人预估了接收者在收到这些赞美时会有多开心。

sentences.en: And we also asked a separate group of people to anticipate how the recipient would feel when they got these compliments.
sentences.zh: 我们还要求另一组人预估接收者在收到这些赞美时的感受。

sentences.en: The observers who imagined complimenting this person every day thought the recipient would get tired of it.
sentences.zh: 那些想象每天都要赞美这个人的观察者认为，接收者会对此感到厌烦。

sentences.en: You know, I get it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我懂。

sentences.en: You love me.
sentences.zh: 你爱我。

sentences.en: Enough.
sentences.zh: 够了。

sentences.en: It turned out the recipients, though, they liked it just as much as the day before.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，接收者和前一天一样喜欢这些赞美。

sentences.en: We didn't see any consistent decrease in how positive they felt receiving the compliment, in part because each one was unique.
sentences.zh: 我们没有观察到他们收到赞美时的愉悦感有任何持续下降，部分原因是每一句赞美都是独一无二的。

sentences.en: And when stuff is different, you don't adapt to that.
sentences.zh: 当事物有所不同时，你就不会产生适应。

sentences.en: It stays good all along.
sentences.zh: 它会一直保持美好。

sentences.en: So you're someone who likes to, you know, walk the talk.
sentences.zh: 所以你是一个喜欢言行一致的人。

sentences.en: And so you took this research finding back to your own family, and you proposed a new Christmas tradition.
sentences.zh: 于是你把这个研究发现带回了自己的家庭，并提议了一个新的圣诞传统。

sentences.en: Tell me what the tradition was that you proposed and how it went down.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你提议的那个传统是什么，以及它是如何进行的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So anybody who is familiar with the Christian tradition will be familiar with the concept of an Advent calendar.
sentences.zh: 任何熟悉基督教传统的人都会熟悉“降临节日历”这个概念。

sentences.en: It's a thing that you get where you open a little tag every day, and there's chocolate behind every day up until Christmas starting December 1St.
sentences.zh: 这是一种你会收到的东西，从12月1日开始，你每天打开一个小标签，每一天后面都有巧克力，直到圣诞节。

sentences.en: Well, this year I decided we would try something else in the family.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今年我决定在家里尝试点别的。

sentences.en: We would do a compliment calendar in my family that followed the same sort of Advent tradition.
sentences.zh: 我们家要搞一个遵循同样降临节传统的“赞美日历”。

sentences.en: But instead of opening up chocolate every day, it would be a compliment every day.
sentences.zh: 但不是每天打开巧克力，而是每天收到一句赞美。

sentences.en: So I asked everybody to write down a compliment about everybody else in the family that they could pass along.
sentences.zh: 所以我让每个人都写下一句关于家里其他人的赞美，以便传达给对方。

sentences.en: And they did four of these so that we could stretch it out through the month.
sentences.zh: 他们写了四轮，这样我们就能把活动贯穿整个月。

sentences.en: So they wrote it down on a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 他们把赞美写在纸条上。

sentences.en: I folded that up, bend it over into a ring, and then strung it together into a chain of these rings.
sentences.zh: 我把它折起来，弯成一个圆环，然后串成一串圆环链。

sentences.en: So every day, you'd tear off one of these rings, open it up, and there would be a compliment.
sentences.zh: 所以每天你都要撕下一个圆环，打开它，里面就是一句赞美。

sentences.en: And how did it go?
sentences.zh: 结果怎么样？

sentences.en: Did the family embrace the idea?
sentences.zh: 家人接受这个主意了吗？

sentences.en: Did they love it?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢吗？

sentences.en: There was not great enthusiasm at the start of this, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我得说，刚开始的时候大家热情不高。

sentences.en: They were pretty confident that this is not going to go well, and I think I'd rather have chocolate instead of these compliments.
sentences.zh: 他们很确信这不会顺利，我想他们宁愿要巧克力也不想要这些赞美。

sentences.en: But once we actually did it, it was great.
sentences.zh: 但当我们真正开始做的时候，效果好极了。

sentences.en: I still have some of those compliments from that first year we did it, sitting in my office at the house.
sentences.zh: 我至今还保留着我们第一年做的时候写下的一些赞美，它们就放在我家的办公室里。

sentences.en: I look at them every day when I'm working at home.
sentences.zh: 我在家工作时每天都会看它们。

sentences.en: I want to switch gears to another kind of social interaction that we often avoid.
sentences.zh: 我想转换话题，谈谈另一种我们经常回避的社交互动。

sentences.en: You had an extraordinary teacher whom you loved very much in high school.
sentences.zh: 你在高中时有一位非常敬爱的老师。

sentences.en: Tell me a bit about him, Nick.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊他吧，尼克。

sentences.en: So I've been a professor since 2001, and even before then.
sentences.zh: 我从2001年起就开始当教授了，甚至在那之前也是。

sentences.en: You know, I was in graduate school for five years, and was in college for five years before that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在研究生院待了五年，在那之前还在大学待了五年。

sentences.en: I've seen amazing teachers over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些年来我见过很多了不起的老师。

sentences.en: But the most amazing teacher I've ever seen, and the best one I've certainly ever had,
sentences.zh: 但我见过的最了不起的老师，也是我肯定遇到过的最好的老师，

sentences.en: was a band teacher at Cedar Rapids Prairie High School in Iowa, which is where I went to high school.
sentences.zh: 是爱荷华州锡达拉皮兹草原高中的一位乐队老师，那是我读高中的地方。

sentences.en: Craig Oni is his name.
sentences.zh: 他叫克雷格·奥尼。

sentences.en: And Mr. Oni was the most passionate teacher I've ever seen.
sentences.zh: 奥尼先生是我见过最有激情的老师。

sentences.en: We would march on the field in competitions, and you could hear Mr. Oni yelling from the stands,
sentences.zh: 我们会在比赛中在场地上行进，你能听到奥尼先生在看台上大喊，

sentences.en: with his own voice, not amplified in any way.
sentences.zh: 用他自己的嗓音，没有任何扩音设备。

sentences.en: And he was just so enthusiastic and encouraging, particularly for a bunch of kids, particularly like me.
sentences.zh: 他总是那么热情和鼓舞人心，尤其是对一群孩子，特别是像我这样的孩子。

sentences.en: We're not the easiest kid to teach.
sentences.zh: 我们可不是那种容易教的孩子。

sentences.en: I did not care to be in band much at all.
sentences.zh: 我根本不在乎参加乐队。

sentences.en: I was mostly there to have fun and screw around.
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间都在那儿玩乐和胡闹。

sentences.en: And he didn't care.
sentences.zh: 但他不在乎。

sentences.en: He brought the best out of us, no matter what.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他都激发了我们最好的一面。

sentences.en: Did you have a chance to tell him that?
sentences.zh: 你有机会告诉他这些吗？

sentences.en: You know, I never have.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从来没说过。

sentences.en: Part of it is that I took him for granted when I was in high school.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是我在高中时把他视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And it wasn't obvious to me just how amazing he was until I spent so many years watching other people,
sentences.zh: 直到我花了这么多年观察其他人，

sentences.en: you know, being amazing teachers in their own right, but still not reaching that level.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们本身也是很棒的老师，但仍然没达到那个水平，我才意识到他有多么了不起。

sentences.en: So it wasn't until I got older that I really appreciated just how great he was.
sentences.zh: 所以直到我年纪大了，我才真正体会到他有多么伟大。

sentences.en: And by that time, he had retired, and I wasn't sure how to reach out and express that to him.
sentences.zh: 而那时他已经退休了，我不知道该如何联系他并向他表达这些。

sentences.en: You once ran a study where you asked volunteers to send a gratitude letter to someone in their lives.
sentences.zh: 你曾经做过一项研究，要求志愿者给他们生活中的某个人写一封感谢信。

sentences.en: I'm assuming, as in the previous examples, most people misperceive the effect this letter would have on the recipients.
sentences.zh: 我假设，和之前的例子一样，大多数人误解了这封信会对接收者产生的影响。

sentences.en: That's part of the thing, too, for me with Mr. Oni, is that it's been so many years
sentences.zh: 这也是我和奥尼先生之间的问题所在，因为已经过去这么多年了，

sentences.en: that reaching out, out of the blue, just feels like it's going to be weird.
sentences.zh: 突然联系他感觉会很奇怪。

sentences.en: What often gets in the way is our concern or anxiety about how the other person might respond.
sentences.zh: 阻碍我们前进的往往是我们对对方可能作何反应的担忧或焦虑。

sentences.en: What exactly will I say?
sentences.zh: 我到底该说什么？

sentences.en: Will I get the words just right?
sentences.zh: 我能把话说得恰到好处吗？

sentences.en: So the depth of appreciation that I feel for Mr. Oni is so intense.
sentences.zh: 我对奥尼先生的感激之情是如此强烈。

sentences.en: Am I going to say that right, or is it not going to do it justice?
sentences.zh: 我能表达得当吗？还是说这根本无法表达我的心意？

sentences.en: So there are all these fears or anxieties that we have about how well we'll be able to do this
sentences.zh: 所以我们对能否做好这件事有各种恐惧或焦虑，

sentences.en: that sometimes hold us back.
sentences.zh: 这有时会阻碍我们。

sentences.en: And what we find is that when we ask people to actually do this,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当我们要求人们真正去做这件事时，

sentences.en: whether it's my MBA students here at the University of Chicago
sentences.zh: 无论是芝加哥大学的MBA学生，

sentences.en: who have asked to do this in a class demonstration for years now,
sentences.zh: 他们多年来一直被要求在课堂演示中这样做，

sentences.en: or just folks out there in the world we ask to do this,
sentences.zh: 还是我们要求世界各地的普通人这样做，

sentences.en: people tend to underestimate how positively their recipient is going to respond.
sentences.zh: 人们往往低估了接收者会作出的积极回应。

sentences.en: They recognize it'll be great, but it turns out this is like one of the best
sentences.zh: 他们意识到这会很棒，但事实证明，这可能是你一生中收到的

sentences.en: letters you'll ever receive in your life.
sentences.zh: 最好的信件之一。

sentences.en: Nick's research shows that we systematically underestimate how much we will enjoy connecting
sentences.zh: 尼克的研究表明，我们系统性地低估了与人建立联系的乐趣，

sentences.en: with people and how meaningful our outreach will feel to others.
sentences.zh: 以及我们的主动联系对他人而言有多么深刻的意义。

sentences.en: But no matter how many times we see this,
sentences.zh: 但无论我们看到多少次这种情况，

sentences.en: no matter how many times the data confirms this,
sentences.zh: 无论数据证实了多少次，

sentences.en: it can still feel as though we'd be better off keeping to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然会觉得独处会更好。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to combat our false intuitions.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨如何克服我们错误的直觉。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Nicholas Epley is a psychologist at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉斯·埃普利是芝加哥大学布斯商学院的心理学家。

sentences.en: His research suggests that every day we have a choice to make.
sentences.zh: 他的研究表明，我们每天都要做出选择。

sentences.en: Do we strike up a conversation with the person sitting next to us on the train or plane?
sentences.zh: 我们是与火车或飞机上坐在旁边的人搭话吗？

sentences.en: Or do we keep our eyes fixed on our phones and laptops?
sentences.zh: 还是把目光锁定在手机和笔记本电脑上？

sentences.en: Do we offer compliments and gratitude to the people who matter in our lives?
sentences.zh: 我们是向生命中重要的人表达赞美和感激吗？

sentences.en: Or do we assume that they already know how we feel?
sentences.zh: 还是假设他们已经知道我们的感受了？

sentences.en: Do we keep our views on sensitive topics to ourselves
sentences.zh: 我们是把对敏感话题的看法藏在心里，

sentences.en: or open ourselves up to difficult but meaningful conversation?
sentences.zh: 还是敞开心扉进行困难但有意义的对话？

sentences.en: Nick, you've said that we face what you call
sentences.zh: 尼克，你说过我们面临着你所说的

sentences.en: approach or avoid decisions all the time in social life.
sentences.zh: 社交生活中无处不在的“接近或回避”决策。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?
sentences.zh: 你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: And what is your advice?
sentences.zh: 你有什么建议？

sentences.en: So I think of this as the choice.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是选择。

sentences.en: Not just every day of our lives, but depending on where we are and what we're doing,
sentences.zh: 不仅是我们生命中的每一天，根据我们身处何地、正在做什么，

sentences.en: sometimes every hour of our lives, every five minutes of our lives.
sentences.zh: 有时是每小时，甚至每五分钟。

sentences.en: And these choices, these social choices, often involve a tension
sentences.zh: 这些选择，这些社交选择，往往涉及一种张力，

sentences.en: between the desire to approach, to connect,
sentences.zh: 即接近、建立联系的渴望，

sentences.en: but also the fears we have that sometimes lead us to avoid other people.
sentences.zh: 以及我们有时会导致回避他人的恐惧。

sentences.en: This approach avoidance dynamic is fundamental to our motivation.
sentences.zh: 这种接近-回避的动态是我们动机的基础。

sentences.en: We see this across species.
sentences.zh: 我们在不同物种中都能看到这一点。

sentences.en: This is kind of how our motivation works,
sentences.zh: 这就是我们动机运作的方式，

sentences.en: there's a tension between these two systems in our own brains.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中的这两个系统之间存在一种张力。

sentences.en: And what we find in our research is that the inputs into those two motivational systems

sentences.en: These were like my kids here,

sentences.zh: 就在他看到屏幕上的字时。

sentences.en: They did not want to do this.
sentences.zh: 其他人开始发出嗡嗡的抱怨声。

sentences.en: A guy in the front swore.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己就像坐在瀑布顶端的一艘独木舟里，

sentences.en: He said, oh, and then issued an expletive
sentences.zh: 我正看着边缘，

sentences.zh: 这情况马上就要失控了。

sentences.en: Everybody else started kind of rumbling and grumbling.
sentences.zh: 我试图在外表上保持冷静，

sentences.en: I felt like I was in a canoe right at the top of a waterfall,
sentences.zh: 但内心却非常紧张，担心这会搞砸。

sentences.en: and I was just seeing over the edge,
sentences.zh: 我硬着头皮告诉他们我们要进行配对，

sentences.en: and this was going to go downhill faSt.
sentences.zh: 我们确实这样做了。

sentences.en: I tried to play it cool on the outside,
sentences.zh: 给了他们印有这些问题的卡片，让他们开始。

sentences.en: but I was nervous this could be on the inside.
sentences.zh: 我当时紧张得要命。

sentences.en: I pushed forward and told him we were going to pair him up,
sentences.zh: 这些人大多数，你知道，大约85%是男性，

sentences.en: and we did.

sentences.en: Gave him cards with these questions on it and let him go.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不想做这个。

sentences.en: And I was just a nervous wreck about this.
sentences.zh: 我当时紧张得要命。

sentences.zh: 但几分钟后，

sentences.zh: 房间里就像是我按下了什么开关，

sentences.en: on their backs or something.
sentences.zh: 或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: They kind of started coming to life.
sentences.zh: 他们开始变得活跃起来。

sentences.en: They were laughing with each other,
sentences.zh: 他们互相谈笑风生，

sentences.en: and I was going to let them talk for 10 minutes,
sentences.zh: 我本来打算让他们聊10分钟，

sentences.en: but at 10 minutes, the room was very loud.
sentences.zh: 但到了10分钟时，房间里已经非常吵闹了。

sentences.en: Everybody was talking.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说话。

sentences.en: They were having a good time,
sentences.zh: 他们聊得很开心，

sentences.en: and there was no way I was going to get them out of those conversations.
sentences.zh: 我根本没法让他们停止交谈。

sentences.en: About five minutes later,
sentences.zh: 大约五分钟后，

sentences.en: I started shouting into my microphone
sentences.zh: 我开始对着麦克风大喊，

sentences.en: that we had just a few minutes left.
sentences.zh: 说我们只剩下几分钟了。

sentences.en: I finally was able to corral them at about 20 minutes
sentences.zh: 最后我在大约20分钟时成功把他们召集起来，

sentences.en: by doing a trick I heard from my kid's kindergarten teacher,
sentences.zh: 用的是我从孩子幼儿园老师那里学来的一招，

sentences.en: counting down very loudly from five.
sentences.zh: 大声地从五倒数到一。

sentences.en: When you hit one, they usually are quiet.
sentences.zh: 当你数到一时，他们通常就会安静下来。

sentences.en: And so I had to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不这样做。

sentences.zh: 让我感到震惊的是，

sentences.en: was the shift in the feeling in that room
sentences.zh: 房间里的气氛发生了转变，

sentences.en: to the end where I could hardly pull them apart.

sentences.en: I saw another guy hugging another guy

sentences.zh: 在他们谈话结束时。

sentences.en: Everybody was shaking hands when they left.
sentences.zh: 每个人离开时都在握手。

sentences.en: The whole mood in that room brightened.
sentences.zh: 整个房间的气氛都变得明快了。

sentences.en: That move from dread to delight at the end,
sentences.zh: 那种从恐惧到最后愉悦的转变，

sentences.en: I'd never seen anything like that happen.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过这样的事情发生。
